lines.japanese: 犬を連れた散歩じゃなくなったので、犬の話をしながらの散歩にしてみた。
lines.english: Since we were no longer taking a dog for a walk, we took a walk while talking about dogs instead.

lines.japanese: 「あいつらさ、なんかナチュラルに肛門とか見せて歩くじゃん。そらもうアレ、よっぽど自信あんだろうな」
lines.english: “They just stroll around with their assholes on display like that’s the most natural thing in the world. Must be mighty proud of them.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、ガムいりますー？」
lines.english: “Dra, would you like some gum?”

lines.japanese: 「実際キレ良すぎだもんな。紙使わねーのにすっきりしてるもんな。そりゃ見せたくもなるよな」
lines.english: “I mean, the cutoff really is incredibly clean. They don't use paper and still come away spotless. No wonder they want to show it off.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、緑茶フラボノイド配合ですよー」
lines.english: “Dra, it contains green-tea flavonoids.”

lines.japanese: 「まあでも、尻尾振って擦りよられると、さすがにちょっぴり愛くるしいとか思っちゃうけどな」
lines.english: “Still, when one wags its tail and comes rubbing up against you, even I have to admit it's kinda adorable.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、分かります分かります。向こうにいたころ、ハンスさんのお宅にいたグレートデンが私によく懐いててですね、もー庭の前を通るだけですーぐ尻尾振って飛びついてくるんですよー」
lines.english: “Yes, I know exactly what you mean. When I lived overseas, the Great Dane at Mr. Hans’s house really took a liking to me. All I had to do was walk past the garden and it would start wagging its tail and jump all over me.”

lines.japanese: 「そそ、アレきっとアレだよな。肛門の綺麗っぷりをアピールしたくて、尻尾ガァー上げてんだよな」
lines.english: “Exactly. That's gotta be why they crank their tails way up. Desperate to advertise just how clean their assholes are.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、クロロフィルも入ってますよー」
lines.english: “Dra, it has chlorophyll too.”

lines.japanese: 暴投まじりな会話のキャッチボールを続けながら、若者で賑わう日曜夜のグローヴ通りまでやって来た。
lines.english: We kept tossing this wildly errant conversation back and forth until we reached Grove Street, bustling with young people on a Sunday evening.

lines.japanese: 俺は鳴が突きだしてきた何個目かの粒ガムを受けとって、上着のポケットに突っこんだ。口の中にはまだ、さっきもらった蜂蜜味の飴玉が残っていた。
lines.english: I accepted the latest pellet of gum Naru held out and shoved it into my jacket pocket. The honey-flavored hard candy she'd given me earlier was still in my mouth.

lines.japanese: 「つーかよ、さっきからおまえよ、話の腰を折るみてーにポンポンぽんぽん菓子よこすんじゃねえよ」
lines.english: “Seriously, what is with you? Quit handing me candy every five seconds like you're trying to snap the conversation in half.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、みたいじゃなくて、まさしく折ってるんですけどー」
lines.english: “Oh, it isn't *like* I'm trying. Snapping it in half is exactly what I'm doing.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに。なんで。おまえ、犬の話とか嫌いなの」
lines.english: “What? Why? You don't like talking about dogs?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、排泄器官以外の話なら喜んで承りますけどー」
lines.english: “I'd be delighted to discuss any part of them other than an excretory organ.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでだよ。古今東西、犬を語るのに肛門は避けて通れねーだろが。てめ、なにカマトトぶってんだよ」
lines.english: “Why the hell not? Since time immemorial, you can't talk about dogs without confronting the asshole. Who are you playing the blushing innocent for?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、グミもありますよー」
lines.english: “Dra, I have gummy candy too.”

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃ肛門の他に犬の話ってなんかあんの」
lines.english: “Wait, are there things to say about dogs besides their assholes?”

lines.japanese: 「はー、そもそも犬の話は必須課題なんですか」
lines.english: “Was talking about dogs a mandatory assignment in the first place?”

lines.japanese: 「そらまぁ、とりあえずなぁ。いや、だってそうだろ。この程度の壁が越えられねーようじゃ、むしろ俺たち自身が負け犬になるって話じゃん」
lines.english: “Well, for now, yeah. Think about it. If we can't clear a little hurdle like this, then we're the ones who wind up the losers—the beaten dogs.”

lines.japanese: 俺は上手いことを言った。
lines.english: I had said something clever.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そうですかー。えー、それではですねー、イギリスのウィーダという作家が著したア・ドッグ・オブ・フレンズという小説をかいつまんで御紹介しますねー」
lines.english: “Ah, I see. In that case, allow me to present an abridged account of *A Dog of Flanders,* a novel by the English author Ouida.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、そうじゃなくてよ。犬の出てくるお話じゃなくて、犬をテーマに世間話をっつーことだよ」
lines.english: “No, no, that's not what I mean. I don't want a story with a dog in it. I mean everyday conversation with dogs as the subject.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、でもいいお話ですよー。泣けてきますよー」
lines.english: “But it's a wonderful story. It will make you cry.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　マジかよ、上等だコラ。砂漠の瞳と呼ばれたこの俺を、泣かせられるもんなら泣かせてみろコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Huh? Bring it on. If you think you can wring a tear from the man they call Desert Eyes, let's see you try.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、時は１８００年代後半、アントワープに程近い小さな村のお話です」
lines.english: “Our story takes place in the latter half of the nineteenth century, in a small village near Antwerp.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ。そんな、知らねー国の埃かぶった与太話で泣けるほど、俺の感受性はガード甘くねーっつうの」
lines.english: “Hah. My emotional defenses aren't so sloppy that some dusty fable from a country I've never heard of can make me cry.”

lines.japanese: 「ある日、主人公のネロ少年は、金物屋に酷使されうち捨てられていた一匹の労働犬を介抱し──」
lines.english: “One day, a boy named Nello nurses a working dog that an ironmonger has abused and abandoned—”

lines.japanese: 「え、うそ、その話知ってる。あ、ちょ、タンマタンマ。うわ、涙腺緩んできた」
lines.english: “Wait, no, I know this one. Hold it, time out. Oh, shit, my tear ducts are already coming loose.”

lines.japanese: 「そして、元気を取りもどしたその犬はパトラッシュと名付けられ──」
lines.english: “And when the dog recovers, he is given the name Patrasche—”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、待て待て。待てって、泣いちゃうって。やっべ、鼻の奥ツーンってしてきたツーンって」
lines.english: “Wait, wait, stop. I'm serious, I'm gonna cry. Oh, shit, the back of my nose is stinging. Really stinging.”

lines.japanese: 「おー、てめソレ反則だろ。ネロはやべーってマジで。あいつ２０世紀最大のトップブリーダーだろ」
lines.english: “Come on, that’s cheating. Nello is dangerous, seriously. That kid was the twentieth century’s greatest dog breeder.”

lines.japanese: 「ネロ、１９世紀ですけどー」
lines.english: “Nello lived in the nineteenth century.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ、いいんだよ、あいつらの友情は歴史さえ凌駕すんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. It doesn't matter. Their friendship transcends history itself.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、ドラさん見かけによらず涙もろいんですねー」
lines.english: “Haah. You're surprisingly quick to tears, Dra.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　たりめーだろ、俺の感受性はハンパねーっつうの。間欠泉のごとき瞳と呼ばれてるっつうの。映画館行くなら、常にハンカチ五枚は持ってくっつうの」
lines.english: “Huh? Of course I am. My sensitivity's off the charts. They call my eyes the twin geysers. I take five handkerchiefs every time I go to the movies.”

lines.japanese: 「どしますー？　やっぱり普通の世間話にしときますー？」
lines.english: “So, what do we do? Go back to regular small talk?”

lines.japanese: 「だな。あーやべやべ、あやうく往来で目から真珠汁こぼすとこだった」
lines.english: “Yeah. Christ, that was close. I almost spilled pearl juice from my eyes in the middle of the street.”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、ドラさん犬とか飼ってますかー」
lines.english: “Let's see... Do you have a dog, Dra?”

lines.japanese: 「おー、ソレいいんじゃねーの。ソレだ、そういう話で行こう」
lines.english: “Yeah, that'll work. That's it. Let's go with that kind of thing.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、飼ってるんですかー」
lines.english: “Oh, you do?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、飼ってねーけどな。まあ、だってほら、俺自身が言わば籠の中のハヤブサみてーなもんじゃん」
lines.english: “No. But then, I'm basically a falcon in a cage myself.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 「だってほら、俺自身が言わば籠の中のハヤブサみてーなもんじゃん」
lines.english: “I said, I'm basically a falcon in a cage myself.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はいはい。上手いです上手いです」
lines.english: “Ah, yes, yes. Very clever. Well done.”

lines.japanese: 「で、おまえン家はやっぱアレか。こんな、トゲトゲの首輪つけたシェパードとかドーベルマンとかが、喉をぐるぐる鳴らしながら庭を徘徊してるわけか」
lines.english: “So your place has got to be like this, right? Shepherds and Dobermans in spiked collars prowling the grounds with growls rumbling in their throats?”

lines.japanese: 「はー、カートゥーンですか私の家。ていうか、うちマンションだから庭ないですよー」
lines.english: “Is my home a cartoon? We live in an apartment. We don't have grounds.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうなん。パルさんがおまえのことエエトコの嬢だって言うから、なんか超でけーお屋敷とか住んでんのかと思った」
lines.english: “Oh. Really? Paru said you were some fancy young lady, so I figured you lived in a gigantic mansion or something.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、それクラスの子にも言われたことあります。どうも知らないうちに私のキャラが出来あがってるみたいでー、やーもー、びっくり仰天ですよねー」
lines.english: “Oh, kids in my class have told me that too. Apparently this whole image of me took shape without me even realizing it. I mean, what a shock, right?”

lines.japanese: 鳴は袖からはみ出た指先に白い息を吐きかけた。
lines.english: Naru blew white breath over the fingertips protruding from her sleeves.

lines.japanese: １１月ももうすぐ終わりだ。何気なく自分のジャケットに触れてみると、意外なぐらい冷たくなっていた。
lines.english: November was almost over. I touched my jacket absently and found it had grown surprisingly cold.

lines.japanese: 「よー。どうする、どっか入る」
lines.english: “Hey. What do you think—want to go inside somewhere?”

lines.japanese: 俺は肩をすぼめて周囲を見回した。コーヒースタンド、フルーツパーラー、イタリアンレストラン。景色としては見慣れてるけど、改めて個々に焦点を絞るとどうにも親近感の湧かない建物ばかりが生えていた。
lines.english: Hunching my shoulders, I looked around. Coffee stand. Fruit parlor. Italian restaurant. The streetscape was familiar enough, but once I considered each place individually, none looked remotely like my kind of establishment.

lines.japanese: 「んー、そうですねー、どっちでもいいですよー」
lines.english: “Mm, sure. Either way is fine with me.”

lines.japanese: どっちでもと言うより、どうでも良さそうに鳴は言った。
lines.english: Naru sounded less like either option was fine and more like she couldn't care less.

lines.japanese: 「なに。寒くねーの」
lines.english: “What, you aren't cold?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そうですよねすみません。いいですよー、あったかいとこ入りましょうかー」
lines.english: “Oh. Right, I'm sorry. Sure, let's go somewhere warm.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、俺じゃなくて」
lines.english: “I didn't mean me.”

lines.japanese: 両手をポケットに入れたまま、並んで歩く小さな体をついっと顎で指した。やつは一瞬口を開けて固まったが、すぐに笑って首を横に振った。
lines.english: Hands still in my pockets, I tipped my chin toward the slight figure walking beside me. Her mouth opened and froze for an instant. Then she quickly smiled and shook her head.

lines.japanese: 「やー、寒いかもですけどー、寒いからこそってゆー空気も嫌いじゃないですしー」
lines.english: “Well, I might be cold, but I kind of like the atmosphere you only get because it *is* cold.”

lines.japanese: 「ほー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: ガキのくせになかなかいい感性してる。
lines.english: Not bad instincts for a kid.

lines.japanese: 「じゃー、そーだな、そこのコーヒー屋でも入ってテラス席とか？」
lines.english: “Then let's see... How about that coffee place? We could sit on the terrace.”

lines.japanese: しかし我ながら上出来だと思った俺の提案に、やつは難色とまでいかないものの微妙な反応を示した。
lines.english: I thought it was a fine proposal myself. She didn't quite object, but her reaction was distinctly lukewarm.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、そのお店よく行くんですかー」
lines.english: “Do you go to that place often, Dra?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　いや、未踏の地だけど」
lines.english: “Huh? No. Completely unexplored territory.”

lines.japanese: 「ですよねー」
lines.english: “I thought so.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに『ですよね』って。ちょっと待って。いまひっぱたくとこか」
lines.english: “Wait, what do you mean, ‘I thought so’? Is this the part where I smack you?”

lines.japanese: 「この辺りでドラさんがよく行くのはどこですか」
lines.english: “Where do you usually go around here?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　あー、そーだな……」
lines.english: “Huh? Well, let’s see...”

lines.japanese: ふたたび俺はこじゃれた景観を見渡した。この中で馴染み深いと言えば、せいぜいが……。
lines.english: Once more I surveyed the tastefully fashionable streetscape. The closest thing here to familiar territory would be...

lines.japanese: 「あの辺とか？」
lines.english: “Over there, maybe?”

lines.japanese: 俺は幅の狭い通りの右側、緩やかなカーブを描きながら上ってゆく白い階段を指した。そう、階段だ。
lines.english: I pointed to the right side of the narrow street, where a white staircase climbed in a gentle curve. Yes. A staircase.

lines.japanese: しかし鳴は気付かずに階段の横、円筒のショウケースに閉じこめられたウサギさんの群れに目を凝らした。
lines.english: Naru failed to notice. Instead, she peered at the colony of little rabbits imprisoned in the cylindrical display case beside it.

lines.japanese: 「はー、雑貨屋ですか」
lines.english: “Oh. The sundries shop?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃなくて」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 俺は人差し指を斜め上に振った。やつは口を開けたまま二階を見上げ、レトロモダンな港町を想わせる紅茶とスイーツの店を眺めた。
lines.english: I tilted my index finger upward. Mouth open, she looked to the second floor and gazed at a tea-and-sweets shop with the retro air of an old port town.

lines.japanese: 「へっ、ティーサロン？」
lines.english: “Huh? The tea salon?”

lines.japanese: 「違うって。その中間。ほら」
lines.english: “No. Between the two. Look.”

lines.japanese: 俺は階段のふもとまで歩いていって、頭の高さぐらいの段を背中越しに指した。
lines.english: I walked to the foot of the stairs and pointed over my shoulder at a step roughly level with my head.

lines.japanese: 「は、階段ですか？」
lines.english: “The—the stairs?”

lines.japanese: 「階段ですよ」
lines.english: “The stairs.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、道行くひとの迷惑ですよう」
lines.english: “What? You'll be in everybody's way.”

lines.japanese: 「いいんだよ。だいたい、俺の活動時間なんてこの辺の店閉まったあとだし」
lines.english: “It's fine. I'm usually active after all these places have closed anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「……ドラさん、コンビニの前で座りこんじゃうひとですか」
lines.english: “...Dra, are you one of those people who squats outside convenience stores?”

lines.japanese: 鳴は語尾を伸ばさずぴしゃりと切って、険しい顔で俺を見上げた。風紀委員か、こいつ。
lines.english: Naru clipped the sentence short instead of drawing out the ending and looked sternly up at me. What was she, a hall monitor?

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫だって。そりゃ、おまえの兄貴みたいなんが固まって座りこんでたらアレだけどさ、俺みたいなクールガイが星空の下ひとりで佇んでる分にはなんも問題ねーじゃん。むしろアートじゃん。超リリカルじゃん」
lines.english: “It’s fine. Sure, if a pack of guys like your brother were squatting there, that’d be one thing. But there’s nothing wrong with a cool guy like me lingering alone beneath the stars. That’s art. It’s totally lyrical.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、けしからんですよー。やー、もー、好感度うなぎくだりー」
lines.english: “Oh, that simply won't do. Dear me, my opinion of you is soaring like a lead balloon.”

lines.japanese: 「いやおまえ、そうは言うけどな。いっぺんやってみって」
lines.english: “Say what you like, but try it once.”

lines.japanese: 「やーですよう」
lines.english: “Nooo.”

lines.japanese: 俺は手を伸ばした。鳴は一歩引いたが、こっちは二歩進んでやつの肩を掴んだ。
lines.english: I reached for her. Naru retreated one step, so I advanced two and caught her by the shoulders.

lines.japanese: 「いいから。これマジいいから。マジ飛ぶから」
lines.english: “Just do it. I'm serious, it's amazing. It'll get you *high.*”

lines.japanese: 「あああ、染まるー、悪色に染まるー」
lines.english: “Aaaah, I'm being corrupted! The bad influence is rubbing off!”

lines.japanese: 「悪じゃねえよばか、これコンクリートジャングルの森林浴なんだよ、ほれっ」
lines.english: “It isn't evil, idiot. This is forest bathing in the concrete jungle. Here.”

lines.japanese: 俺は男の腕力で強引にやつの体を旋回させ、下から四段目にスカートの尻を打ちこんだ。
lines.english: I used brute strength to wheel her around and plant her ass, skirt and all, on the fourth step from the bottom.
“Mrrr...”

lines.japanese: 「どうよ」
lines.english: “Well?”

lines.japanese: 「はー、お尻が冷たいです」
lines.english: “My bottom's cold.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は不服そうに俺を見上げていた。
lines.english: Naru looked up at me with quiet resentment.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、最初はそんなもんか。でも向いてると思うんだよ、おまえ」
lines.english: “Well, that's how it is at first. But I think you've got a real gift for it.”

lines.japanese: 「向いてるとどうなんですか」
lines.english: “And what happens if I do?”

lines.japanese: 「ひみつ」
lines.english: “Secret.”

lines.japanese: 「試しに今度、ひとりンときやってみ。ただそのへん座って、ぼけーっとしてりゃいいんだよ」
lines.english: “Try it sometime when you're alone. Just sit down somewhere and let your mind go blank.”

lines.japanese: 「ぼけーっ」
lines.english: “Blaaank...”

lines.japanese: 「うお、すげえ。すげほら、ちょー似合ってる。いまおまえ、風吹いてるよ、マジ追い風だよ。でも口は閉じてていいから」
lines.english: “Whoa, incredible. Seriously, look at you—that suits you perfectly. The wind's at your back. A real tailwind. You can close your mouth, though.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、あのー、これいったい何やってんだろーって自問したくなりません？」
lines.english: “Doesn't this make you want to ask yourself what on earth you're doing?”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、おまえが言うのかよ」
lines.english: “Whoa. *You're* asking that?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、でもいいんだよ。それもアリなんだよ。そういう『何やってんだろー』も含めてこう、なんかいろいろ入ってくんだよ、プチ悟り得られんだよ。ヒントは耳を開け」
lines.english: “No, no, that's part of it. That whole ‘what the hell am I doing?’ thing goes into the mix, and then all kinds of stuff starts flowing into you. You attain a little pocket-sized enlightenment. Here's a hint: open your ears.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、自己啓発的というか、信仰宗教の勧誘ライクな話ですねー」
lines.english: “This sounds partly like self-help and partly like recruitment for some religious cult.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、たしかにそーなんだけどさ。でもトリップ出来りゃおもしれーよ。出来ねえやつは出来ねえと思うけど、おまえならマジ、なんか素質ある気すんだよ。だから勧めてんだし」
lines.english: “Well, yeah, I guess it does. But if you can trip, it's fun. Some people just can't, but I seriously think you've got the knack. That's why I'm telling you to try.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんは出来るんですかー」
lines.english: “Can you trip, Dra?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、そういう気分のときはな」
lines.english: “When the mood takes me.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁー、トリップ出来ると何が入ってきますかー」
lines.english: “Ooh. And when you trip, what comes flowing in?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、なんつったらいいかなあ……新しい世界？　いや、違げえな。知ってるのに知らなかったもの？」
lines.english: “Uh, how do I put this... a new world? No, that's not it. Things you knew, but never knew you knew?”

lines.japanese: 「……いや、いいわ。なんか、言葉にしちゃうとぜんぜん大したことじゃねーし、実感しなきゃ意味ねーから。だから言わねーどく」
lines.english: “...No, forget it. Put it into words and it sounds like nothing, and unless you feel it for yourself, it doesn't mean a thing. So I'm keeping quiet.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なんですかそれ。もー、ここまで引っぱっといてー」
lines.english: “What? After stringing me along all this way?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ悪り悪り。でもほんとコレ、俺のとっときなんだよ。つーか、ぶっちゃけひとに教えんの、おまえが初めてだし」
lines.english: “Yeah, sorry, sorry. But this really is one of my best-kept secrets. Honestly, you’re the first person I’ve ever taught it to.”

lines.japanese: 「あらやだ、そんな風に言われるとちょっと有難い気がしてきましたよ」
lines.english: “Oh my. When you put it that way, I almost feel honored.”

lines.japanese: 「だろ。感謝しとけよ、てめ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Damn right. Be grateful, asshole. I’ll fucking kill you, you bastard.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、ありがとうございます。えーと、にわかには賛同しかねる話ですが、いつか機会があればやってみます」
lines.english: “Yes, thank you. I can't say the proposal has won me over on the spot, but if the opportunity presents itself, I'll try it someday.”

lines.japanese: 「おー。でも次やるときは、パンツ見えねーように気ぃ付けろよ」
lines.english: “Sure. Next time, though, make sure nobody can see your panties.”

lines.japanese: パンツ女は無言でそっと目を落とした。
lines.english: The panty girl silently lowered her gaze.

lines.japanese: 「いえー、見えてないですよー？」
lines.english: “No one could see them.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、見えてないですじゃなくて。こっちから見えてたっつう話」
lines.english: “Don’t tell me they weren’t visible. I’m telling you *I* could see them.”

lines.japanese: 「いえもー、ぜんっぜん見えてないですよー」
lines.english: “No, no. They were completely invisible.”

lines.japanese: 「だから。見えてたかどうかはおまえが判定することじゃないから」
lines.english: “That's not for you to decide.”

lines.japanese: 「パースペクティブの転換ですよー」
lines.english: “It’s a shift in perspective.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、意味分かんねーけど、たぶんそれ使い方間違ってっから」
lines.english: “I have no idea what you mean, but I’m pretty sure you’re using that wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そだー、ドラさんチョコいりますー？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Dra, want some chocolate?”

lines.japanese: 鳴は赤い顔のまま立ちあがって、照れかくしみたいにはたはたと両手でケツの汚れを払った。
lines.english: Still red in the face, Naru stood and fluttered both hands over her backside, dusting it off as though to hide her embarrassment.

lines.japanese: 「カカオのポリフェノールでピロリ菌をぴろり撃退ですよー」
lines.english: “Cocoa polyphenols send *H. pylori* packing—bye-lori!”

lines.japanese: 「あーもー、ええっつうの。話の腰を折られるたんび菓子もらってたら、一年後には俺ン家にヘンゼルとグレーテルが迷いこんでるっつうの」
lines.english: “Oh, enough already. If you give me candy every time you derail the conversation, a year from now Hansel and Gretel'll be getting lost in my apartment.”

lines.japanese: でもまあ、そうは言いつつ、俺は鳴のてのひらに載っているダイスチョコを拾いあげてやった。
lines.english: Even as I complained, I plucked the cube of chocolate from Naru's palm.

lines.japanese: 上着のポケットには、やつから贈られた個別包装のアメやらガムやらが、すでにたんまり詰まってる。俺は新たな収穫物をジーンズの尻ポケットへ入れようとした。
lines.english: My jacket pocket was already bulging with individually wrapped candy and gum she'd pressed on me. I went to stow this latest harvest in the back pocket of my jeans.

lines.japanese: 指先に硬い紙の感触。なんだろう。チョコと取りかえるように、それを引っぱりだしてみた。
lines.english: My fingertips met stiff paper. What was that? I pulled it out, trading places with the chocolate.

lines.japanese: 「あー。なんだ、これか」
lines.english: “Oh. This thing.”

lines.japanese: 皺だらけの黒いカード。きのうガード下で咲夜とかいう佐久間にむりやり受けとらされたまま、ゴミ箱へ移すのを忘れていた。
lines.english: A black card, crumpled all to hell. Sakuma—Sakuya, whatever his name was—had forced it on me beneath the tracks yesterday, and I’d forgotten to transfer it to the trash.

lines.japanese: 「はー、なんですかー、それ」
lines.english: “Oh. What's that?”

lines.japanese: 鳴が口を開けたまま、ひょこっと首を伸ばして覗きに来た。
lines.english: Naru, mouth hanging open, poked her head over for a look.

lines.japanese: 「さあ。欲しけりゃやるけど」
lines.english: “Beats me. You can have it if you want.”

lines.japanese: どうせ捨てるもんだったし。
lines.english: I was only going to throw it away.

lines.japanese: 「えー、ゴミだったらいりませんよ」
lines.english: “No thank you. I don't want your trash.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、やるからコレ。ゴミかどうかは自分の目で確かめてみろよ」
lines.english: “That's why I'm giving it to you. See for yourself whether it's trash.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、なんなんですか教えてくださいよー」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. What is it? Tell me.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、おま、見んなっつの。極秘情報なんだよコレ。正式に譲渡が行われるまで見せらんねーんだよ」
lines.english: “Hey—don't look, I said. This is top-secret intelligence. I can't show it to you until the transfer is official.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、じゃーいいです。結構です。いりません」
lines.english: “Then never mind. No, thank you. I don't want it.”

lines.japanese: 「まーまー、遠慮すんなって。な、菓子いっぱいもらったから。な、ほんのお礼代わりにコレ」
lines.english: “Come on, don't be shy. You gave me all this candy, right? Consider this a little token of my gratitude.”

lines.japanese: 「結構ですってばー。なにがお礼代わりですか、もー、明らかに捨てる気まんまんの保存状態じゃないですかそれー」
lines.english: “I said no, thank you. What kind of gratitude is that? One look at the state of it and anyone can tell you've been waiting for a chance to throw it away.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえな、そういう外見でゴミとかクズとか決めつける先入観が子供の繊細な心をねじ曲げんだっつーの。ほら、いいから黙ってもらっとけって」
lines.english: “Listen. That kind of prejudice—deciding something's trash or worthless from the way it looks—is what twists a child's delicate heart. Come on. Shut up and take it.”

lines.japanese: レジの前で支払い権を主張しあうおばはん同士みたいに、俺たちは一枚の紙片（ていうか、もはや一本の紙筒）を押しつけあった。
lines.english: Like two old ladies at a register battling for the right to pay, we thrust the scrap of paper—or rather, by now, the paper tube—back and forth at each other.

lines.japanese: しかしこのままでは埒があかないので、俺はやつの注意を逸らすべく、唐突に真横を向いた。
lines.english: This was getting us nowhere, so I abruptly turned my head to one side to draw her attention away.

lines.japanese: 「あ、全米が痩せた脅威のサプリ」
lines.english: “Oh! The miracle supplement that made all America lose weight.”

lines.japanese: 「まじで？」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「なわけねーだろ」
lines.english: “Of course not.”

lines.japanese: すかさず俺は鳴のポケットに紙屑をねじこんだ。
lines.english: I seized the opening and crammed the scrap into Naru's pocket.

lines.japanese: 「ああーっ！　もぉー、ちょー……あふん」
lines.english: “Aaah! Oh, come on... ahn.”

lines.japanese: 「あたっ」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 「キショい声出すな」
lines.english: “Don’t make creepy noises.”

lines.japanese: 「戸惑ってる戸惑ってる」
lines.english: “You’re flustered. You’re flustered.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「あどけない少女の唇から零れた、刹那の女に胸が震えましたね」
lines.english: “For one fleeting instant, womanhood spilled from an innocent girl’s lips. Your heart trembled.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おいガキ。あんま滑稽なことほざくな。もっといろんな声で鳴かすぞコラ」
lines.english: “Hey. Listen, kid. Quit talking ridiculous shit, or I'll find a dozen new ways to make you squeal.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: やつはいきなり頬に手を添え、一度ゆっくり俯いてから、はにかむように俺を見上げた。
lines.english: She suddenly laid a hand against her cheek, slowly lowered her eyes, then looked shyly back up at me.

lines.japanese: 「……なんだよ」
lines.english: “...What?”

lines.japanese: 「やーですよう、そんなー」
lines.english: “Oh, you mustn't…”

lines.japanese: 「え……ちょっと待って。なんで照れてんのおまえ」
lines.english: “Wait… Why are *you* embarrassed?”

lines.japanese: 「もードラさんってば、まだ早いですってー。困りますよう。都合のいい女にされるから最後まで色はかけるなって、パルさんにも言われてますしい」
lines.english: “Oh, Dra, it’s much too soon. What am I supposed to do? Paru told me never to take the flirting all the way, or a man will start treating me like I’m easy.”

lines.japanese: 「パル？」
lines.english: “Paru?”

lines.japanese: 俺は思わずクレープ屋の方角へ向かってつぶやいた。
lines.english: Without thinking, I muttered the name toward the crêpe stand.

lines.japanese: 「ババアてめ、なにくだらねーこと吹きこんでんだよ」
lines.english: “You old hag. What kind of nonsense are you teaching her?”

lines.japanese: やつはいまごろ、腹を抱えてげらげら笑っているような気がした。
lines.english: I had a feeling she was doubled over and roaring with laughter right about now.

lines.japanese: 「安い女じゃないですよー」
lines.english: “I am not a cheap woman.”

lines.japanese: 「テンション高けぇなあ」
lines.english: “You are *way* too excited.”
